summary: Milestone 2026.04.99's supplied operational closeout slice was short and orchestration-bound: 10 minutes total wall time, 2 completed items, and a 5 minute average. The only material slow path was the 10 minute arXiv Bundle v10 slot, which correctly waited on exp1269 critical paper fixes and then compiled the v10 bundle. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout with only 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization; gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes, so there were no material zombie processes. Pre-flight checks were seconds-scale, not the bottleneck. The recoverable loss is serial publication/docs closeout and unused GPU scheduling capacity.

slowest_experiments.title: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: This was the only material critical-path item in the supplied timing slice. It could not run until exp1269 fixed all five critical paper issues, then it compiled docs/arxiv-paper/main.tex with tectonic and wrote results/carnot-arxiv-v10-20260504.tar.gz. The time was legitimate gate plus TeX/package work, not GPU compute.

slowest_experiments.title: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: No material wall-clock cost was visible in the provided timing. The docs pass was tied to the arXiv bundle but did not independently bottleneck this slice.

bottlenecks_identified: The operational closeout was dominated by one serial publication gate: exp1270 could only run after exp1269 critical paper fixes were terminal.
GPU utilization was inefficient from a milestone-scheduling perspective. scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json at 2026-05-04T19:43:32Z showed both RTX 3090s idle at 4 MB and 0% utilization.
No material zombie GPU processes were present. The monitor reported an empty process list and no warnings; the 4 MB allocations were negligible driver/context residue.
Pre-flight was not the bottleneck in this slice. Conductor rows for exp1269 and exp1270 showed 81 tests passing in 8.24s and 7.89s, far below the 10 minute wall-clock closeout.
The arXiv/docs critical path was too serial. Bundle compilation and documentation reconciliation were closeout tasks instead of being prepared asynchronously once exp1269 completed.
Doc reconciliation was cheap for the supplied timing row, but ops/changelog.md contains multiple .99 operational-retro refresh entries, which shows the broader process is not idempotent.

Structured timing remains too coarse. The supplied slowest list has minute buckets, so gate wait, pre-flight, TeX execution, and docs reconciliation have to be inferred from artifacts and conductor rows.
improvements_suggested: Run independent CPU/data tasks and any GPU-capable validation lane while publication packaging waits on paper gates.
Promote gpu_monitor.py output into scheduler decisions: if both GPUs are idle and queued work can use live models, start a DualGPURunner lane or emit an explicit blocked reason.
Cache TeX dependencies and add a narrow arXiv bundle preflight target so exp1270 can fail fast on missing tooling before it enters the critical path.
Record per-experiment timing fields in result artifacts: queued_at, started_at, gated_wait_s, preflight_s, execution_s, docs_reconcile_s, and finished_at.
Make operational retro, changelog, and roadmap updates idempotent for a milestone so repeated recovery passes do not accumulate near-duplicate entries.
Emit structured blocked artifacts for gated tasks immediately; exp1271-style prior_failures blocks should cost one terminal artifact, not repeated operator interpretation.
Batch docs reconciliation after terminal artifacts are written, while keeping roadmap insertion duplicate-aware.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A 30% saving is realistic for the next similar closeout: roughly 10-15% from overlapping independent CPU/GPU work with publication gating, 5-8% from cached TeX/pre-flight state, 5% from structured gate-block artifacts, and 5% from idempotent batched docs reconciliation. On a 10 minute slice that is only a few minutes, but the same fixes matter more when the milestone has many gated tasks.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Run GPU-capable experiments in a dedicated DualGPURunner lane whenever gpu_monitor.py reports both cards idle.
Add first-class conductor timing fields separating gate wait, pre-flight, execution, and docs reconciliation.
Make docs and roadmap reconciliation idempotent and batch it after terminal artifacts exist.

gpu_utilization.assessment: Inefficient from a resource-scheduling perspective. The closeout itself was CPU/docs-bound, but the idle DualGPU capacity should have been used for independent model-bearing work if any remained queued.

zombie_process_assessment.basis: scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json at 2026-05-04T19:43:32.914625+00:00 reported no GPU processes and no warnings.
zombie_process_assessment.note: The 4 MB allocations on each RTX 3090 do not meet the monitor's zombie definition and were not material throughput waste.

preflight_assessment: Not a bottleneck for this closeout slice. The relevant .99 conductor rows showed focused 81-test checks taking 8.24s for exp1269 and 7.89s for exp1270.
doc_reconciliation_assessment: The in-process docs item was listed as 0 minutes, so it did not materially slow this slice. The broader doc process should still be tightened because repeated .99 operational-retro refresh entries show reconciliation is not idempotent.
parallelization_assessment: exp1270 itself could not be parallelized before exp1269 completed, but documentation reconciliation and other non-publication work in the 1268-1281 milestone range could have run in parallel lanes. The next milestone should keep one CPU/docs lane and one GPU/model lane active rather than waiting for publication packaging to clear.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: exp1270 took 10 minutes and was the only material slow item. It was slow because it sat on the paper/arXiv critical path after exp1269 and performed actual TeX bundle compilation plus packaging. The docs item registered 0 minutes.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at 4 MB and 0% utilization. The closeout work was CPU/docs-bound, but the milestone scheduler still left available GPU capacity unused.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes: No. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings, so there were no material zombie processes wasting VRAM.
question_answers.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. exp1270 was gate-dependent, but docs reconciliation and other non-publication tasks in the .99 range could have overlapped with CPU or GPU-capable validation lanes.
question_answers.was_the_pre_flight_test_suite_a_bottlene: No. Available .99 conductor rows show focused pre-flight checks in seconds, not minutes.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Partly for this slice, because the docs row was 0 minutes. Process-wide, no: repeated .99 changelog refreshes show reconciliation should be idempotent and batched.
question_answers.what_tooling_would_speed_up_the_next_mil: GPU-aware scheduling from gpu_monitor.py, DualGPURunner-by-default for queued model work, cached TeX/pre-flight targets, structured per-experiment timing, immediate blocked artifacts for unmet gates, and idempotent docs reconciliation.

meta_reflection: The main operational lesson is that .99 was no longer losing hours to failed compute in the requested closeout slice; it was losing small but repeatable minutes to serial closeout mechanics. That is a better failure mode, but it still compounds. The next milestone should make the conductor prove that idle GPUs are either used or explicitly blocked, and should make docs updates deterministic rather than a repeated agent chore.
